Registering a suspend delay and responding to suspend and resume signals is not very straightforward so putting it all into a client class makes it easier to encapsulate and test. BUG=chromium:906523 TEST=unit tests Change-Id: I3956092fd7929324c19e64191eb6eb67b959821e Signed-off-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1437934 Reviewed-by: Jeffrey Kardatzke <jkardatzke@google.com>

vm_tools: concierge: Suspend VMs when the device is suspended In order to ensure that clock drift during a device suspend does not trigger a softlockup in the guest VM watchdog, suspend VMs when the device is suspended and resume them when the device resumes. The Service class already had a power manager dbus proxy so replace it with the PowerManagerClient, which better encapsulates the complexity of dealing with suspend and resume attempts. BUG=chromium:906523 TEST=start an allmodconfig build in the linux source directory and then run `powerd_dbus_suspend --wakeup_timeout=300` on the host. Observe the logs to see crosvm changing the VM run status to "Suspending" and then back to "Running". Also observe that the VM does not crash on resume. Change-Id: Ia9c3ef10ccf3cbd90e9bfc1f500f2854504f5ea8 Signed-off-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1437935 Reviewed-by: Jeffrey Kardatzke <jkardatzke@google.com>

vm_tools: Add UNIX socket support to cicerone for plugin VM This allows plugin VMs to communicate with cicerone. This is done by mounting the /run/vm_cicerone/client folder into the plugin VM at the location /cicerone. In that directory will be a UNIX socket called host.sock which the plugin VM should use to send messages back to cicerone. When sending these messages, the 'container_token' in the protobufs should be obtained from the path /cicerone_token/token inside the plugin VM. Upon startup, the plugin VM should read the token, open a gRPC server at unix:///cicerone/<token>.sock that implements the Garcon interface, then make a connection to /cicerone/host.sock and invoke the ContainerReady gRPC call. That will cause cicerone to connect back to <token>.sock for making calls into the plugin VM. Valid calls that the plugin VM can make on the host are: ContainerReady, UpdateApplicationList and OpenUrl. Valid calls that cicerone will make on the plugin VM are: LaunchApplication and GetIcon. BUG=b:122837958 TEST=Plugin VM can read token, tast vm.CrostiniStartEverything and unit tests pass Change-Id: I72037a825d01a25e01d099213a8a65bb99da0add Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1436764 Commit-Ready: Jeffrey Kardatzke <jkardatzke@google.com> Tested-by: Jeffrey Kardatzke <jkardatzke@google.com> Reviewed-by: Jeffrey Kardatzke <jkardatzke@google.com>

tast: Add VirtualKeyboardSuggestions test. The virtual keyboard gets its word suggestions from a service called the decoder. However, this decoder is built elsewhere, so we don't really have any tests that make sure the decoder works with the UI. This test ensures that the virtual keyboard does indeed load the decoder correctly and that the decoder can provide suggestions to the virtual keyboard. There is a quirk with decoders however. Decoders ignore what the user types until it is fully loaded. There is no easy way to wait for the decoder to load, so we just have to keep pressing keys until the decoder provides suggestions. Until we have a good way of waiting for the decoder to load, we'll just do this hack.
